messages.author: 1115f9030ac79b49
messages.subject: Slope coefficients
parts:
Dear all, 

I am analyzing the body shape of fish in several habitat types during ontogeny and in order to evaluate shape variability I use regression for procrustes shape variable (procD.lm) and pairwise comparison, but I want to extract the slope coefficients for each habitat. Is this possible? and where do you find them since the model?

Thank you in advance,

Best regards,

Mathieu Reynaud

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Slope coefficients
parts:
Dear Mathieu,

There are multiple ways to get coefficients from a procD.lm fit: $coefficients, $LM$coefficients, and the coef() function. The former two mean that if you have a procD.lm fit, e.g., myFit, then myFit$coefficients or myFit$LM$coefficients will reveal the coefficients.  The function is better if you also want to perform tests using RRPP; e.g.,

coef(myFit) # reveals coefficients
coef(myFit, test = TRUE) # performs test on coefficients

Hope this helps!

Mike

messages.author: fbfd20ce829c6c6c
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Slope coefficients
parts:
Mathieu, 

coef(, test = TRUE) is a test of the regression coefficients for each term in the model. This is separate from pairwise because pairwise is not meant to compare regression coefficients, but instead compares pairwise statistics (e.g., means, slopes, vector correlations, variances) between levels of some factor. I encourage you to look at the help pages of each ?coef.lm.rrpp and ?pairwise should help.

Best,
Bryan
